findings.title: subtotal NPEs on null list or null element instead of failing fast
findings.evidence: the loop iterates `items` and dereferences `item.unitPrice()` with no null checks, while the record constructor sets an IllegalArgumentException precedent for bad input
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit guard at method entry: Objects.requireNonNull(items, "items required") and skip/reject null elements with IllegalArgumentException so callers get a consistent contract instead of a NullPointerException mid-loop.

findings.title: taxRate is unvalidated: null NPE, negative or percent-scale values accepted
findings.evidence: `BigDecimal tax = cents(subtotal.multiply(taxRate));` uses taxRate directly with no null check, no non-negative check, and no documented unit (fraction vs. percent) — a caller passing 8.25 instead of 0.0825 silently produces a 100x tax figure
findings.recommendation: Require non-null, non-negative taxRate (e.g. requireNonNull plus compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) >= 0) and document the expected unit in the method signature or javadoc, or accept a percentage type with a dedicated conversion.

findings.title: Per-line rounding means subtotal can differ from rounding the exact sum
findings.evidence: each line is rounded to SCALE via `cents(...)` before being added, e.g. two items of unitPrice 0.005 quantity 1 yield 0.02 instead of 0.01; the rounding policy is undocumented so the divergence is invisible to callers
findings.recommendation: State the rounding policy explicitly (per-line rounding is a common invoice convention) in javadoc, or accumulate exact products and round once at the end if the exact-sum policy is intended; add a test pinning the chosen behaviour.

findings.title: unitPrice only null-checked: negative and over-scale prices pass silently
findings.evidence: the compact constructor rejects null unitPrice but never checks sign or scale, so negative prices (credits) and values with more than two decimals are rounded away without warning
findings.recommendation: Add a sign/scale check (e.g. unitPrice.compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) >= 0, and optionally unitPrice.scale() <= SCALE) or document that discounts and sub-cent prices are intentional, so HALF_UP rounding of negatives is a deliberate, tested decision.

findings.title: No tests pin the money rounding behaviour
findings.evidence: no test commands were run and the diff adds no tests for `value.setScale(SCALE, ROUNDING)`, leaving the half-cent edge case and the per-line vs. total rounding policy unverified
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests covering: half-cent line values, empty list, quantity 1 with sub-cent unit price, multi-line accumulation, and tax rounding such as subtotal 0.05 with taxRate 0.1.

findings.title: Local variable shadows the subtotal method name
findings.evidence: `BigDecimal subtotal = subtotal(items);` reuses the method name for a local, making the following line read ambiguously between the field and the method
findings.recommendation: Rename the local to e.g. netTotal or subTotalAmount to avoid shadowing the public method name.
